newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices down, Honolulu sells.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices down, Honolulu sells.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were off as much as 1/2 point in spots as Smith Barney Inc brought the day's largest new issue to market, traders said.
"It feels ugly," one trader said, quoting the cash market down 3/8 to 1/2.
A second trader said the market seemed only about 1/4 lower, despite a Treasury market where the long bond dropped 5/8 to 96-2/32 to a 7.07 percent yield.

"People are getting pretty tired of this," one trader said, lamenting the municipal market's on-again, off-again rally of recent weeks. "We did the rally through seven percent again on a good Friday number, and got crushed on back again."
Smith Barney Inc tentatively priced $100 million Honolulu, Hawaii, general obligation bonds at a top yield of 5.80 percent in 2016.
Bear Stearns & Co said it tentatively priced $30 million Nevada Housing Division bonds at a top yield of 6.35 percent in 2028.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract was down 18/32 to 112-15/32 while the T-bond was off 20/32 to 107-14/32. The MOB spread was 161 ticks.
A stronger-than-expected U.S. August housing starts report overshadowed the decline in weekly jobless claims.

August starts were the strongest since March 1994, rising 4.5 percent to an annual rate of 1.525 million units compared to the average trade estimate of 1.445 million units and against July's rate of 1.46 million units.
Meanwhile jobless claims for the week ended September 14 fell to 329,000. Economists on average were looking for claims to fall to 335,000.
